signed_rows.behavior: The network tests are an integration tier: registered, strict markers on, left out of the default pytest run, and run by an integration gate in .loop/config.toml.
signed_rows.fails_when: the default uv run pytest collects a test that adds the okf marketplace from GitHub, the marker is not registered or --strict-markers is off, or .loop/config.toml has no gate running uv run pytest -m integration

signed_rows.behavior: In the integration tier a network error is retried up to two more times; any other failure is reported at once; three network failures still fail.
signed_rows.fails_when: a test failing twice with 'Could not resolve host' then passing is reported as failed or runs more than three times, a test failing with another message is rerun, or one failing three times with a network error is reported as passed or skipped; or a test whose install fails with a network error is not retried because the failure surfaces later as another error

signed_rows.behavior: Every test in tests/test_plugin_install.py that adds the okf marketplace from GitHub carries the integration marker.
signed_rows.fails_when: such a test lacks the marker

signed_rows.behavior: Every kmctl plugin install or update call in tests/test_plugin_install.py asserts its exit code with the command output.
signed_rows.fails_when: any such call's result is not checked with exit_code == 0 and its output

signed_rows.behavior: The default suite and the integration tier both pass.
signed_rows.fails_when: uv run pytest or uv run pytest -m integration fails
signed_rows.command: uv run pytest -q -m "not integration or integration"

resigns.reason: follow the python-testing rule: integration tier out of the default run, its own gate, retry on network errors only
plan round 1 review: every install asserts its output so the network error reaches the retry hook
